rows.name: createSignal
rows.note: One state per call: the setter's argument (or an updater's return) is what the getter's calls read.

rows.name: createResource
rows.note: One resource per call: what the fetcher settles to, or what mutate receives, is what the accessor reads. The source (or what it returns) is the fetcher's first parameter, and refetch's argument its second's `refetching`. The source may be left out.

rows.name: createMemo
rows.note: The call makes an accessor that yields what its callback returns.

rows.name: createSelector
rows.note: The call makes a predicate: calling it tests a key against what its source returns, and yields a boolean.

rows.name: children
rows.note: The call makes an accessor that yields what its callback returns.

rows.name: createDeferred
rows.note: The call makes an accessor that yields what its callback returns, later.

rows.name: createRoot
rows.note: The call's value is what its callback returns.

rows.name: mapArray
rows.note: The call makes an accessor of a list: the callback takes each item of what the source returns, and the list holds what it returns.

rows.name: indexArray
rows.note: The call makes an accessor of a list: the callback takes each item of what the source returns as an accessor, and the list holds what it returns.

rows.name: For
rows.note: `createMemo(mapArray(() => props.each, props.children))`: the child takes each item as a value and an accessor of its index, which no prop supplies; the list holds what it returns.

rows.name: Index
rows.note: `createMemo(indexArray(() => props.each, props.children))`: the child takes an accessor of each item and its index as a number, which no prop supplies; the list holds what it returns.

rows.name: Show
rows.note: Renders its child while `when` is truthy; a function child takes an accessor of the value, or with `keyed` the value itself.

rows.name: Switch
rows.note: Renders the first `Match` whose `when` is truthy (the `Match` row says what its child takes), else `fallback`.

rows.name: Match
rows.note: Inside a `Switch`: renders its child while `when` is truthy and no earlier `Match` is; a function child takes an accessor of the value, or with `keyed` the value itself.

rows.name: ErrorBoundary
rows.note: Renders its children; when they throw, a function `fallback` takes the error and a `reset` function, which no prop supplies, and renders what it returns.

rows.name: Suspense
rows.note: Renders `fallback` while a resource its children read is loading, then its children; it calls no function it is given.

rows.name: Dynamic
rows.note: `createDynamic(() => props.component, others)`: calls the `component` prop with the other props and renders what it returns.

rows.name: untrack
rows.note: The call's value is what its callback returns.

rows.name: batch
rows.note: The call's value is what its callback returns.

rows.name: on
rows.note: The call returns a new function: calling it runs the callback with what the source returns, and yields the callback's return.

rows.name: splitProps
rows.note: The split objects carry the props they are given.

rows.name: mergeProps
rows.note: The merged object carries every object it is given.

rows.name: createEffect
rows.note: The framework runs the callback for what it does. The call itself has no value.

rows.name: createRenderEffect
rows.note: The framework runs the callback for what it does. The call itself has no value.

rows.name: createComputed
rows.note: The framework runs the callback for what it does. The call itself has no value.

rows.name: onMount
rows.note: The framework runs the callback for what it does. The call itself has no value.

rows.name: onCleanup
rows.note: The call returns the function it is given, and the framework runs that function when its owner is disposed.

rows.name: createStore
rows.note: One store per call: the setter's argument (or an updater's return, or a value at a path of keys) is what the store reads.

rows.name: unwrap
rows.note: The plain object is the store it is given.

rows.name: createMutable
rows.note: The mutable store carries the object it is given.

rows.name: createAsync
rows.note: The call makes an accessor that yields what its callback returns.

rows.name: createAsyncStore
rows.note: The call makes an accessor that yields what its callback returns.

rows.name: useNavigate
rows.note: Calling the function it returns sends the page to that URL: the value leaves the program.

rows.name: useSearchParams
rows.note: Calling the setter it returns writes the page's query string: the value leaves the program.

rows.name: query
rows.note: The call returns the function it is given, wrapped: calling the result runs it with the same arguments.

rows.name: cache
rows.note: The call returns the function it is given, wrapped: calling the result runs it with the same arguments.

rows.name: action
rows.note: The call returns the function it is given, wrapped: calling the result runs it with the same arguments.

rows.name: useAction
rows.note: The call returns the function it is given, wrapped: calling the result runs it with the same arguments.

rows.name: useSubmission
rows.note: One submission per call: its `result` is what the action's function returns, and its `input` the arguments of each call of the action.

rows.name: makePersisted
rows.note: The persisted pair is the signal or store pair it is given.

rows.name: debounce
rows.note: The call returns the function it is given, wrapped: calling the result runs it with the same arguments.

rows.name: throttle
rows.note: The call returns the function it is given, wrapped: calling the result runs it with the same arguments.

rows.name: leading
rows.note: The call returns the function it is given, wrapped: calling the result runs it with the same arguments.

rows.name: leadingAndTrailing
rows.note: The call returns the function it is given, wrapped: calling the result runs it with the same arguments.

rows.name: createQuery
rows.note: The query's value is what its `queryFn` returns.

rows.name: createInfiniteQuery
rows.note: The query's value is what its `queryFn` returns.

rows.name: useQuery
rows.note: The query's value is what its `queryFn` returns.

rows.name: createMutation
rows.note: `mutate(x)` calls the `mutationFn` with `x`.

rows.name: useMutation
rows.note: `mutate(x)` calls the `mutationFn` with `x`.
